The following is not in any form a well written or thought out argument but a rant of the consistent problems I've had the displeasure of personally experiencing.  

Game got way worse since recent updates. Their trying to keep the game interesting and adding new characters with unique skills and balancing patches, but like every "hero" type game, the most recent works are just obscenely busted. 

Almost every character has some form of ability that just doesn't work against others. You would think that means just swap to another that can counter them, but they haven't added those counters yet. 

EX: I play a lot of Angela, but almost every one of her abilities can be countered by some of the most common picks. Her flight - which is her base movement form - can be canceled by grounding from several characters. Her ability to dive can also be cancelled by the same thing, meaning you can't swap to melee type in critical moments. The grounding also lasts several seconds, in which you're just screwed, because you're still in "flight" but also "grounded" so her movement is extremely slow.  

Cont: Angela's stab also can't pierce anyone with a "shield" or "armor", so is completely negated by characters like Mr. Fantastic, Devil Dino, Thing, etc. This gets compounded when other heroes can add this status as a buff to others, or momentarily get it when activating their own abilities. Making what seems to be her primary ability almost useless lest you're up against the perfect opposing team. Even her ultimate can easily be ignored, like Gambit has a cleanse that completely undoes the chaining of Angela's ultimate. 

All this wouldn't be so bad if there was genuine balancing - Moonknight's ultimate is instant and cannot be blocked or cancelled. Scarlet Witch's stuns can now cancel other ultimate's but she also gets a "shield" for her own so she cannot be blocked or cancelled. 

Overall it's clear that whenever they do a "balancing" the only thing they balance is the complaints from people playing that character. They take no consideration to how other players will be interacting with that character other than to make the original person feel better about themselves by having no choice but to die. 

All that and not to forget - Rivals intentionally has a matchmaking system called "♥♥♥♥ you." If you win too many games in a row, or do too well at all, the system will cobble together team after team to make your night a living hell. Only to then apologize and give you the easiest matches possible - I'm talking games where you genuinely question if the opponents aren't bots. 

The overall content also hasn't changed at all since release. The announcer only has like 2 voice lines, so every match you hear the same thing, again and again and again and again. It gets so old so fast, alongside they haven't added new maps or the choice of which mode you'd like to play in. There's only quickplay, comp, and the event mode. Quickplay doesn't let you choose if you want a push the cart or hold the point, nor what maps you do or don't want. Just pray you get a good map and the mode you like, otherwise sucks to suck.

I’ve put 127 hours into Marvel Rivals and genuinely tried to give this game every chance because the actual gameplay can be a lot of fun.

My biggest problem is that the game just doesn’t feel consistent or fair enough for me to take seriously competitively.

Damage and hit registration can feel completely different from one situation to another, enemies sometimes survive things I’ve seen kill the same characters countless times before, and there are attacks that seem to connect when they shouldn’t or fail to register when they clearly should.

Then there’s the matchmaking. Way too many games are complete blowouts. It often feels less like the better players won and more like the match was stacked heavily in one team’s favor from the beginning.

I know the game has buffs, healing, shields, damage reduction, falloff, counters, and plenty of other mechanics. I’ve played enough to understand that. I also can’t prove exactly what is happening behind the scenes. I can only judge the experience I’m having, and after 127 hours I don’t trust the consistency of the game anymore.

I even gave it one final chance and spent most of the last two days playing again. I came away feeling exactly the same.

It’s a shame because I genuinely enjoy Marvel Rivals. But if you’re looking to seriously invest yourself into competitive play or tournaments, I personally couldn’t recommend doing that in its current state.

For now, I’m done with it.

It really sucks to thumbs down a game I think has a lot of great mechanics. Rivals was one of my favorite games to play with friends and every season made me more and more excited to see what comes next, but it's hard for me to ignore the pattern in front of me. There is a constant pattern of exclusion and disrespect to the black characters in the game, and it has gotten to a point where I cant help but question its intentionality. I dont mind more popular characters getting skins, but any time Storm is meant to be a part of a set, she gets put in Epic tier where others are legendary. Most recently is the summer skins, where the outcry from the community forced their hand to promise changes, but this is the same story with the wedding skins from a few seasons before. I think the devs do a fine enough job keeping an eye on the community, making changes to improve the game, but also seeing the culture the game creates. We know they are online, considering how many emotes and sprays reference pop culture and memes. For them to do nothing after the dozens of missteps with their black characters is at its least harmful, lazy, and at most, a direct spit in the face to the black player base. 

I reference Storm a lot because she's probably the most glaring example, but the other black characters also get this treatment. before we could play Blade he was in chains, and the first time we see Moon Girl, she is getting arrested. A team that cares does not let patterns like that happen. Moon Girl not being included as a part of Devil Dinosaur could be reasonably explained, but within the context of everything else, It doesn't feel like something they did because it was necessary. Considering Jubilee is a vampire and Rouge has "Chronovium" powers, I'm positive the dev team could have found a way to include her as a real character. If they really wanted to, they would.

I think things can change, maybe Storm will get a rework so she's picked more. Maybe the next black character they introduce wont be imprisoned immediately. Whatever they do, for me to recommend this game, I would need to see a pattern of trying to do better, not just an instance or two of pacifying people you disrespect.

Storm has been here day one and the fact that they treat her as a second class citizen is so odd. The game has changed so much since release and she is fundamentally an outdated character. The same could have been said about Black Widow. That was until recently where BW was almost completely reworked so now she dominates in online matches. You don't give Storm a Legendary win screen until fan outcry and when you do, you don't give her a fun beach moment like everyone else. You make it a part of lore that Black Panther and Storm are married and you don't give them any special win screens or animations like you did for the other white couples in the game.
You add Devil Dinosaur, but not Moon Girl. For my friends, the final straw was the second slate of Egyptian skins. You are willing to give multiple white characters ancient Egyptian skins, but only to white characters. You give everyone Egyptian skins EXCEPT THE WOMAN RAISED IN EGYPT. Reminds me of how no Black Characters got disco skins. That is fine. Its just black people who invented Disco is all.

The latest updates have lost sight of that as it is no longer the fun teamgame that it was before. Characters with independent and aggressive playstyles get buffed or added to the roster, while characters with co-operative and defensive playstyles get nerfed. Matches in the past were fun but nowadays we're chasing that feeling while only experiencing frustration with the gameplay loop the game is heading into (self-sustaining high damage dealing characters outclassing a team with balanced roles). 

The latest content update seems to have double downed on this approach as they deviated from the double character release per 'season', which usually had a high/medium damage dealing character paired with a tankier character or a supportive character, and sometimes both a tankier and supportive character paired together. This season releasing only a high damage dealing character with considerable self-sustain, and further balancing the game around characters with similar playstyles (neglecting tankier, supportive, and more cautious damage dealers).

For players who like to play solo, independently from their in-game team, this game is building up to be a great experience. For players who are interested in teaming up (with friends) and performing well in any of the roles besides high damage dealing characters, don't even bother. 
This experience could have been had in the earlier versions of the game, but there's no way to rollback or modify public matchmaking rules to have such a gameplay loop again. The most fun can be had by hosting a private match with friends where you can ignore the experience the game seems to be balancing around and do your own thing, but at that point why not play a different game where you can have fun experiences in public matchmaking.

[h1][b][i]"Marvel Rivals"[/i][/b][/h1]
[h2][u]1. First Impression[/u][/h2]
Upon first entering the game, I was simply overwhelmed by the sheer volume of information presented to me. Beyond the initial tutorial on game mechanics, I was immediately introduced to numerous limited-time events and special features. It wasn't until the second day that I had a rough idea of which buttons were essential and which ones weren't — not to mention getting familiar with the full roster of heroes :) That’s where I encountered the game's biggest plus: all heroes are available right from the start.
[h2][u]2. Gameplay & Variety[/u][/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Frequent updates[/b]. Updates felt frequent and meaningful. These updates ranged from simple balance tweaks to the release of new heroes, cosmetic items, maps, or even entirely new limited-time PvE modes. In short, players certainly won't get bored.
[*][b]Character roles[/b]. The entire roster is divided into three role groups — Vanguard (Tank), Duelist (DD), and Strategist (Healer) — defined not just by their names but by their unique abilities.
[*][b]Team-Ups[/b]. An additional feature that adds even more variety to the gameplay. Depending on combinations with other characters — whether they are currently on your team or not — your character can gain additional abilities, which may be further empowered by the presence of specific heroes.
[*][b]Variety of characters and abilities[/b]. This is another huge plus for the game. Characters generally fall into two categories: ranged and melee. However, their unique abilities add further depth. For instance, Spider-Man can zip across the map, isolating or eliminating foes with rapid ability combos; Groot can build up multiple walls to block incoming fire or cut enemies off from constant healing; Doctor Strange can help his team cover great distances via portals; and my personal favorite, Emma Frost, can simply shut down most opponents' ultimate abilities while in diamond form. You can only imagine how unique every match feels with 6 vs 6.
[*][b]Game modes[/b]. The game offers short-duration PvE modes and a wider variety of PvP modes. In some, you must dominate specific positions, while in others, you have to escort a payload to a target point within a set time limit. There is even an 18v18 mode for truly chaotic, all-out brawls :). Additionally, a ranked mode is available, allowing you to climb the ladder and face off against more experienced opponents. 
[*][b]Match duration[/b]. You don't need to spend nearly an hour to finish a match. Matches usually last around 20 minutes, which is a big plus for me.
[*][b]Double pick of the same hero[/b]. It removes one of the common frustrations in hero-based games: having your preferred character taken by another player from your team.
[/list]
[h2][u]3. Audio[/u][/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Audio[/b]. The sounds and lines characters shout when unleashing their ultimate abilities are incredible! They give you goosebumps every time — whether it’s your hero or your opponent using them.
The voice lines accompanying standard abilities are also well-crafted.
[/list]
[h2][u]4. Visual Fan Service[/u][/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Fan service[/b]. Characters and their cosmetics often stay very true to the original comic book designs. Even when something new is created, the visuals are likely to appeal to the gaming fanbase — which is more likely to align with Asian aesthetic standards. And from what I can see, everyone is happy with that :)
[/list]
[h2][u]5. Personal experience[/u][/h2]
[list]
[*]Thanks to my background in previous shooters, I didn't face major difficulties with my initial matches. My first hero was Black Widow (in the Duelist/DD role), and I was lucky enough to have teammates who could fill the other necessary roles for a smooth game. Consequently, I quickly secured my first MVPs in Quick Play modes. However, I was surprised to later discover that she was considered one of the worst heroes at the time.
[*]After logging over 100 hours, I was confident playing any role my team needed to secure a win. Need a Vanguard, Duelist, or Strategist? Just say the word — I can be that. Eventually, I reached the Diamond III rank, after which I decided to unlock every possible achievement so I wouldn't have to return to the game — since reaching the absolute peak on the leaderboard wasn't my goal.
[*]The biggest downside throughout the game wasn't that I was sometimes teamed up with complete beginners. I understood that, since I had been in their place not long ago. The real issue was toxic ruzzian players with microphone access who would intentionally throw the match whenever things didn't go their way.
[*]I was personally surprised to find that in Quick Play mode, I frequently encountered bots — on both my team and the opposing one — that stood out due to their distinctive camera movement, which would lock onto enemies. Which are making the match way easy.
[/list]
[h2][u]6. My Advice[/u][/h2]
Don't main only one hero. Build a small pool of 2–3 reliable heroes per role. As your hero can be be picked by teammate or banned by enemy.
[h2][u]7. Final Verdict[/u][/h2]
After more than 100 hours and reaching Diamond III, I can say that Marvel Rivals successfully kept me engaged far longer than I initially expected. Its biggest strengths for me are the variety of heroes, team-based gameplay and constant content updates. The main issues were toxic teammates and the occasional presence of bots in Quick Play. Despite that, [b]I definitely recommend[/b] it.
